title: Butterfly Identification
description: Sample custom JSON deck for identifying notable butterfly species by wing patterns.

cards.name: Monarch Butterfly
cards.subtitle: Danaus plexippus
cards.description: Famous for its multigenerational annual migration across North America. Caterpillars feed exclusively on milkweed, sequestering cardenolide toxins that make adults unpalatable to predators.
cards.keyFeatures: Tawny-orange wings with bold black veins and double rows of white spots along black borders.

cards.name: European Peacock
cards.subtitle: Aglais io
cards.description: A colourful butterfly found throughout temperate Europe and Asia. When threatened, it flashes its four dramatic eyespots to startle birds, while its underside resembles dead dark leaves for camouflage.
cards.keyFeatures: Rusty-red wings with a striking blue-and-black eyespot on each of the four wing corners.

cards.name: Menelaus Blue Morpho
cards.subtitle: Morpho menelaus
cards.description: An iridescent Neotropical butterfly whose brilliant metallic-blue wing color comes from microscopic nanostructures on the wing scales that diffract light rather than pigment.
cards.keyFeatures: Iridescent electric-blue dorsal wings with dark margins; brown underside with bronze eyespots.

cards.name: Old World Swallowtail
cards.subtitle: Papilio machaon
cards.description: A large yellow-and-black butterfly distributed across the Northern Hemisphere. It features prominent hindwing tails and a brick-red eyespot near the inner rear angle of the hindwing.
cards.keyFeatures: Creamy-yellow wings with black vein markings, blue submarginal band, hindwing tails, and red eyespot.
